title: ChatGPT takes 88% of identifiable House AI spending
friendlyTitle: ChatGPT is Congress’s main paid AI tool
summary: A CNBC analysis of U.S. House disbursement records found ChatGPT represented about 88% of identifiable AI-tool spending in the year to March 31. Staff reported using AI for legislative summaries, briefing memos, constituent responses, research and communications, though the records exclude free and bundled tools.
friendlySummary: Public records show that most clearly named AI spending by U.S. House offices went to ChatGPT. Staff use it for research, summaries and messages.
whyItMatters: AI is becoming routine knowledge-work infrastructure even inside institutions deciding how it should be governed. The concentration also shows how quickly one vendor can become the default before procurement, evaluation and oversight mature.
friendlyWhyItMatters: This shows AI is becoming a normal office tool, even where the rules for using it are still being developed.
